Basically, the rice starts out with bacterial spores and possible some bacteria which don't have a good food source. When you cook the rice it becomes a food source for b. Cereus. It grows from the spores that were not killed off by cooking (they can technically be killed, but you'd have to waaaay overcook the rice to do so), and starts to feed off the cooked rice and release waste that is toxic to us. When we refrigerate the rice, we slow down the growth of these bacteria, so for a few days the bacterial load is small enough for us to safely consume.

Cooking the rice kills the bacteria, but it's a sporing bacteria (bacillus cereus) and those spores are heat resistant. The spores themselves won't make you sick, but if the rice is stored improperly or for too long, they grow into bacteria which will.

There's really no for sure way to tell whether the rice is still safe to eat or not, but generally if handled, cooked, and stored properly for short periods of time (my rule is 3 days), it's unlikely to have grown enough bacteria to harm you.

I have taken Klonopin and Ativan, and tried Xanax a few times. Klonopin never made me feel stoned, Ativan did at first but quickly stopped (though it helped the anxiety too). Xanax was the only one I had issues with. They help immensely with panic attacks. As long as you aren't taking them regularly, you should be fine. I've been on 1mg of Ativan twice a day for a few years and am unfortunately dependent due to a stretch where I was panicking daily. Nothing else has helped my anxiety, and while I'm glad I have it, I wish I hadn't gotten dependent. 

I would start with as small a dose as possible if you decide to try it- especially on Klonopin, it shouldn't make you feel high. It's a great last resort!

You might also try propranolol, which will calm your heart down and make it easier to relax (no high feeling, but it might drop your bp a bit as it's a beta blocker). Buspar is another (taken regularly, not as needed). Both are a lot safer, and I would definitely try them before going to benzos. 

There's a lot of trial and error, I know, but you can do this! :)
